title: [FEATURE] Interactive TUI mode: Sticky input bar at the bottom
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing requests](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20label%3Aenhancement) and this feature hasn't been requested yet
- [x] This is a single feature request (not multiple features)

### Problem Statement

Currently, the CLI operates as a standard REPL stream. This means the input prompt moves up and down depending on the length of Claude's output.

When Claude generates a long response or code block, the input cursor often gets lost or pushed out of view. It is inconvenient to visually track the input position while reading the scrolling content. It feels less like a modern chat interface and more like a traditional command stream.

### Proposed Solution

I would like to request a **TUI (Text User Interface) mode** or a layout update where:

1.  **Sticky Input:** The input field is fixed/pinned to the bottom of the terminal window.
2.  **Scrollable History:** The conversation and code outputs scroll in the viewport above the input bar.

This is similar to how modern CLI tools (like `lazygit`, `gh dash`) or standard chat applications interface with the user.

### Alternative Solutions

_No response_

### Priority

Low - Nice to have

### Feature Category

Interactive mode (TUI)

top_comments.author: jhwheeler
top_comments.body: This is a pain point for me as well. For example, Claude presents a plan, and I have comments to this plan. Either I need to scroll back and forth between each point in the plan and the input, checking what it says and giving me feedback one at a time; or I need to have Claude save the plan to a file, which I then edit in nvim and then tell Claude to check those. The latter is a decent workaround but it involves a lot more steps.

top_comments.author: jhwheeler
top_comments.body:
> https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=47183970

This looks nice, but isn't exactly addressing the issue at hand. What we are talking about is the input, not the original prompt. If I ask Claude to do code review, then I have to scroll up to see what the code review says, choose the first finding, scroll down to address it, then scroll back up, etc. instead of being able to just type in the input as I have the scrolled up output visible.
